svg.aria-label: One Claude Code request drawn as an ordered vertical strip of segments: the system prompt (built-in plus appended), with the environment and git snapshot embedded inside it by default; tool schemas; memory files sent as a separate user message; the skill listing; then the conversation so far. A bracket marks the system prompt, tool schemas and memory segments as the cached prefix reused at cache-read price. A leader shows that the flag --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections relocates the embedded environment and git snapshot out of the system prompt and into the first user message instead.
svg.text: REQUEST ASSEMBLY ORDER AND THE CACHED PREFIX
1. System prompt (built-in + appended)
built-in base prompt: ≈2,200 tokens
appended via --append-system-prompt: ≈550 tokens
4. Environment / git snapshot — embedded inside segment 1 by default
cwd, platform/OS, git branch + status, current date ≈280 tokens
moved out only by --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections
combined ≈3,030 tokens enter segment 1 by default
(≈280 of these relocate when the flag above is set)
2. Tool schemas
JSON schema for every registered tool
(Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Agent, ...)
≈3,400 tokens
3. Memory files — sent as a user message
CLAUDE.md (global) + project .claude/CLAUDE.md
+ .claude/rules/*
≈1,100 tokens — also where the flag's relocated facts land
5. Skill listing
name + description + when_to_use per enabled skill
≈900 tokens (50 skills)
6. Conversation so far
prior user/assistant/tool turns — grows every turn, no fixed figure
CACHED PREFIX — REUSED AT CACHE-READ PRICE
--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections
--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections
By default, per-machine facts (cwd, platform/OS, git branch & status, date) are
baked inside segment 1 itself, so segment 1 fails to byte-match across machines.
This flag moves them out of segment 1 and into the first user message instead,
letting the rest of segment 1 stay identical everywhere and cache-hit across machines.
in cached prefix this turn (segments 1-3)
dynamic, not cache-stable — segment 4's inset nested in segment 1 by default; segments 5-6 standalone
leader — the flag relocates segment 4 out of segment 1 and into segment 3 (first user message)
